workload.name: Burst queue
workload.description: A burst of 15 identical jobs per runner, all queued at the same instant, each holding its runner for 60 seconds. Queue time shows how fast a provider absorbs a spike: how quickly it scales, and the concurrency limits of the plan this account is on. Runs on its own, never alongside another suite, in shards of one runner per provider, one shard after another (a provider's x64 and arm64 runners never share a shard, since some providers cap concurrency per account).
workload.shards: one runner per provider per shard (a provider's x64 and arm64 runners in different shards)

runners.label: ubuntu-24.04-arm
runners.note: Standard 4 vCPU arm64 runner GitHub gives public repositories.

runners.label: runs-on={run_id},family=r8a.xlarge,image=ubuntu24-full-x64,ssh=false,retry=false,env=demo,extras=tmpfs
runners.note: Same AMD Turin CPU as runson-m8a-x64 with twice the RAM; /tmp, /home/runner and /var/lib/docker live in memory (extras=tmpfs).

suiteNotes.docker: With tmpfs, /var/lib/docker lives in RAM: a PostHog image build outgrows the 32 GB this machine shares between the tmpfs and the build itself, and the runner runs out of memory. r8a.2xlarge (64 GB) has the room.

suiteNotes.burst: Jobs started in waves as earlier ones finished: the plan this benchmark account is on caps how many run at once, so this queue measures that cap, not how fast the platform scales.

suiteNotes.node: bun install fails on Avrea every time: bun's download of the drizzle-orm registry manifest arrives cut short ("PackageFailedToParse"), on three attempts from an empty cache, while curl on the same runner fetches it complete. The typecheck never starts.
